articles.title: DEEP SKY OBSERVING
articles.summary: This document provides a deep sky observing list compiled by Mark Wagner for the February 2007 third quarter to new moon period. It features a selection of primary (easy) and secondary (more difficult) celestial targets, organized from north to south and within a comfortable right ascension range for viewing. The list includes galaxies, globular clusters, planetary nebulae, and open clusters, with brief descriptions for each.

articles.title: About this dwarf planet Pluto
articles.summary: This article discusses the reclassification of Pluto as a dwarf planet, offering an alternative perspective to public 'hand-wringing' by highlighting Pluto's small size and low density compared to other planets. It draws parallels with historical reclassifications, such as Ceres from planet to asteroid and Earth's demotion from the center of the universe, to emphasize that scientific understanding evolves. The author details the International Astronomical Union's (IAU) three criteria for defining a planet, specifically addressing common misconceptions about the 'clears its orbit' rule.

articles.title: The Last 31 Days In Astronomy
articles.summary: This article compiles significant astronomical news from December 2006 to January 2007, detailing discoveries such as early universe objects by Spitzer, liquid lakes on Titan, and a 3D dark matter map by Hubble, alongside updates on the STS-116 mission and Mars rovers. It also provides an in-depth explanation of Pluto's reclassification as a dwarf planet, outlining the new criteria and a broader planetary categorization system that includes Earth as a "rocky dwarf."

articles.title: NASA Space Place
articles.summary: The article highlights the growing trend of polar flights between the US and Asia, driven by efficiency, and the associated risks posed by space weather. Solar storms can cause issues like radio blackouts, navigation errors, and radiation exposure for flight crews on these routes. To mitigate these risks, NOAA and NASA are deploying advanced GOES satellites, including the upcoming GOES-R, to enhance space weather forecasting and ensure safer air travel.

articles.title: Solar System Stats for February 2007
articles.summary: This article provides detailed astronomical data for solar system objects (planets and Sun) for February 2007, including their Right Ascension, Declination, distance, magnitude, and apparent size, adapted from reputable astronomical handbooks. It also offers a guide for amateur astronomers on the visibility and observational challenges for planets during the month, highlighting Saturn as the main attraction and noting the New Horizons spacecraft's close encounter with Jupiter at month's end.

articles.title: SJAA Donations are Tax-Deductible
articles.summary: This article reminds members that donations to SJAA, a 501(c)(3) charity, are tax-deductible, including annual dues. It also highlights an upcoming auction in April where items donated for sale are deductible at their full fair market value, offering members an opportunity to convert items into tax deductions. Members are advised to consult their tax advisor for specifics.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) operates a loaner scope program, making over 20 telescopes available to its members, managed by Mike Koop. This article details the current status of these scopes, categorizing them as available, recently loaned out, or on extended loan, complete with borrower information, due dates, and instructions for borrowing or joining a waiting list.
